html:
The Huari or Wari Empire was a state that grew from the Ayacucho basin in the central Andes of Peru from around 600 CE and came to cover much of highland and coastal Peru. It lasted about 500 years, until around 1100. The chart's Wari bar shows the same state.

Its capital, Huari, near modern Ayacucho, was a large city of walled stone compounds. Wari ruled through planned administrative centres linked by roads, such as Pikillacta near Cusco. Many scholars see these roads, centres and farming terraces as a model that the Inca later followed.

Wari lived at the same time as Tiwanaku near Lake Titicaca, and the two shared a religious art built around a staff god figure. Wari was once thought to have grown out of Tiwanaku; today they are seen as separate states. On the coast it came after the Moche and Nazca.

Finds keep coming. In 2008 archaeologists found a Wari settlement near Chiclayo, much further north than any known before, and in 2023 a Wari ritual complex about 1,200 years old in Arequipa.
